questions.title: What is the main purpose of database transactions?
options: A. To group operations into a single unit of work
questions.explanation: Transactions ensure that multiple operations are executed as a single atomic unit of work.
questions.source_text: What is the main purpose of database transactions?

questions.title: Which SQL command is used to permanently save changes made in a transaction?
questions.explanation: The COMMIT command saves all changes made during the transaction.
questions.source_text: Which SQL command is used to permanently save changes made in a transaction?

questions.title: Which SQL command is used to undo changes made in a transaction?
questions.explanation: ROLLBACK undoes all changes made during the current transaction.
questions.source_text: Which SQL command is used to undo changes made in a transaction?

questions.title: Which isolation level allows dirty reads?
questions.explanation: READ UNCOMMITTED allows dirty reads, meaning uncommitted changes can be read.
questions.source_text: Which isolation level allows dirty reads?

questions.title: Which isolation level prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads?
questions.explanation: READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads but does not prevent non-repeatable reads.
questions.source_text: Which isolation level prevents dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads?

questions.title: Which isolation level prevents both dirty reads and non-repeatable reads but allows phantom reads?
questions.explanation: REPEATABLE READ prevents dirty and non-repeatable reads but phantom reads may still occur.
questions.source_text: Which isolation level prevents both dirty reads and non-repeatable reads but allows phantom reads?

questions.title: Which isolation level provides the strictest consistency guarantees?
questions.explanation: SERIALIZABLE provides the highest isolation, ensuring transactions behave as if executed sequentially.
questions.source_text: Which isolation level provides the strictest consistency guarantees?

questions.title: In Python's sqlite3 module, which method begins a transaction implicitly?
questions.explanation: Executing any SQL statement implicitly begins a transaction unless autocommit mode is enabled.
questions.source_text: In Python's sqlite3 module, which method begins a transaction implicitly?

questions.title: Which phenomenon occurs when a transaction reads the same row twice and gets different values?
questions.explanation: A non-repeatable read happens when a row is modified by another transaction between reads.
questions.source_text: Which phenomenon occurs when a transaction reads the same row twice and gets different values?

questions.title: Which phenomenon occurs when new rows appear in a query result during repeated reads?
questions.explanation: Phantom reads occur when new rows are inserted by another transaction during repeated queries.
questions.source_text: Which phenomenon occurs when new rows appear in a query result during repeated reads?

questions.title: What is the primary purpose of database migrations in Python projects?
questions.explanation: Migrations are used to apply and track schema changes over time in a controlled manner.
questions.source_text: What is the primary purpose of database migrations in Python projects?

questions.title: Which popular Python library provides migration support alongside ORM features?
questions.explanation: Alembic is the migration tool commonly used with SQLAlchemy for schema evolution.
questions.source_text: Which popular Python library provides migration support alongside ORM features?

questions.title: In Django, which command is used to generate new migration files?
questions.explanation: The makemigrations command generates migration files based on model changes.
questions.source_text: In Django, which command is used to generate new migration files?

questions.title: Which command in Django applies migrations to the database?
questions.explanation: The migrate command applies migration files to update the database schema.
questions.source_text: Which command in Django applies migrations to the database?

questions.title: In Alembic, which command is used to create a new migration script?
questions.explanation: The alembic revision --autogenerate command generates a new migration script based on model changes.
questions.source_text: In Alembic, which command is used to create a new migration script?

questions.title: Which file in an Alembic project stores the migration history?
questions.explanation: Alembic stores migration scripts in the versions/ directory to track schema changes.
questions.source_text: Which file in an Alembic project stores the migration history?

questions.title: What is the purpose of the 'downgrade' function in Alembic migration scripts?
questions.explanation: The downgrade function reverts the schema to a previous state, undoing applied changes.
questions.source_text: What is the purpose of the 'downgrade' function in Alembic migration scripts?

questions.title: In Django migrations, what does the 'dependencies' attribute specify?
questions.explanation: Dependencies specify which migrations must be applied before the current one.
questions.source_text: In Django migrations, what does the 'dependencies' attribute specify?

questions.title: Which Alembic command is used to apply all pending migrations?
questions.explanation: The alembic upgrade head command applies all pending migrations up to the latest revision.
questions.source_text: Which Alembic command is used to apply all pending migrations?

questions.title: Why are migrations important in collaborative projects?
options: A. They allow consistent schema changes across environments
questions.explanation: Migrations ensure that all developers and environments share the same database schema evolution.
questions.source_text: Why are migrations important in collaborative projects?

questions.explanation: The relationship() function defines relationships between ORM models, such as one-to-many or many-to-many.

questions.title: What is a session in a web application?

questions.explanation: Sessions store user-specific data across multiple HTTP requests, since HTTP itself is stateless.

questions.title: Why should passwords never be stored in plain text?
options: B. They are slow to compare
C. They can be easily compromised if leaked
questions.explanation: Storing passwords in plain text is insecure; hashing protects users even if the database is compromised.
questions.source_text: Why should passwords never be stored in plain text?

questions.title: Which function is commonly used to hash passwords in Python web apps?
questions.explanation: bcrypt provides a secure, salted hashing mechanism suitable for passwords.
questions.source_text: Which function is commonly used to hash passwords in Python web apps?

questions.title: What is the purpose of CSRF protection?
options: C. Prevent unauthorized actions from authenticated users
questions.explanation: CSRF protection ensures that requests come from trusted sources and not from malicious third-party sites.
questions.source_text: What is the purpose of CSRF protection?

questions.title: What happens when a user logs out of a session-based application?

B. The session data is invalidated or destroyed
C. The user account is deleted
questions.explanation: Logging out invalidates the session so it can no longer be used for authenticated access.
questions.source_text: What happens when a user logs out of a session-based application?
